nodes.title: Client Interaction
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Clients ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Edge and API ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Core services ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design ~62b69ece~ous processing ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Storage § text#0

content.markdown:
Both clients use the same public HTTPS API and have minimal business logic, primarily input checks. They upload photos directly to object storage using signed URLs to bypass our services for large files.

**From the source:** short-lived

nodes.title: API Gateway Functions
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Clients ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Edge and API ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Core services ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design ~63b6a061~ous processing ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Storage § text#1

content.markdown: The API Gateway handles all client requests, performing TLS termination, access token validation with the auth service, and rate limiting (120 requests/min/account). It routes requests to the appropriate service. If the auth service is unreachable, requests are rejected. Photo bytes are served by the CDN, not the gateway.

nodes.title: Auth Service Role
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Clients ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Edge and API ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Core services ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design ~60b69ba8~ous processing ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Storage § text#2

content.markdown: The Auth Service manages access tokens, accounts, and sessions.

nodes.title: Upload Service Process
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Clients ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Edge and API ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Core services ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design ~61b69d3b~ous processing ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Storage § text#3

content.markdown: The Upload Service provides signed upload URLs, records new photos in the metadata database as 'processing' upon completion, and publishes a 'PhotoUploaded' event to the message queue.

nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Clients ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Edge and API ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Core services ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design ~66b6a51a~ous processing ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Storage § text#4

content.markdown:
**Feed Service Function**

The Feed Service constructs user feeds by reading photo metadata from the metadata database and stores pre-built feed pages in the cache.

**From the source:** ready-made

**Feed Update and Notifications**

The Feed Service subscribes to 'PhotoReady' events to add photos to followers' feeds and notifies followers via a push notification provider if notifications are enabled.

**From the source:** push-notification

nodes.title: Media Processing Workflow
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Clients ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Edge and API ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Core services ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design ~67b6a6ad~ous processing ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Storage § text#5

content.markdown: Media processing workers subscribe to 'PhotoUploaded' events. For each event, they retrieve the original photo from object storage, generate three thumbnail sizes (150, 640, 1080 pixels), store them in object storage, and update the photo status to 'ready' in the metadata database. A 'PhotoReady' event is then published.

nodes.title: Event Queue Resilience
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Clients ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Edge and API ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Core services ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design ~65b6a387~ous processing ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Storage § text#7

content.markdown: The message queue retains events for up to 7 days, ensuring that worker outages only delay, but do not lose, uploads. Photos that repeatedly fail processing remain in the 'processing' state and are not displayed in feeds.

nodes.title: Object Storage Contents
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Clients ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Edge and API ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Core services ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design ~5ab69236~ous processing ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Storage § text#8

content.markdown: Object storage stores original photos and their thumbnails. Originals are immutable and never overwritten.

nodes.title: Metadata Database Role
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Clients ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Edge and API ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Core services ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design ~5bb693c9~ous processing ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Storage § text#9

content.markdown: The metadata database is the authoritative source for photo existence and stores follow relationships and photo records, including their processing status.

nodes.title: Cache Functionality
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Clients ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Edge and API ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Core services ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design ~497e5f83~us processing ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Storage § text#10

content.markdown: The cache stores ready-made feed pages for 60 seconds. It's a speed optimization; losing cached data makes feeds slower but doesn't affect correctness.

nodes.title: System Overview
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Clients ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Edge and API ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Core services ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design ~487e5df0~us processing ⨁ Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Storage § text#11

content.markdown: The Pinhole system is designed with a clear separation of concerns, utilizing a public API for clients, an API Gateway for request management, specialized core services, and asynchronous processing for media. Storage is distributed across object storage, a metadata database, and a cache, each serving a distinct purpose.

content.label: Main data flow: posting a photo
content.takeaway: Photo posting involves client upload, service processing, event-driven updates, and follower notification.

nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Main data flow: posting a photo § shape#0

content.label: 1 · Client requests signed URL & uploads photo

nodes.title: Client Uploads Photo
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Main data flow: posting a photo § text#0

content.markdown: The client requests a signed URL from the upload service and directly uploads the original photo to object storage.

nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Main data flow: posting a photo § shape#1

nodes.title: Upload Service Action
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Main data flow: posting a photo § text#1

content.markdown: The upload service marks the photo as 'processing' and publishes a `PhotoUploaded` event.

nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Main data flow: posting a photo § shape#2

nodes.title: Media Processing
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Main data flow: posting a photo § text#2

content.markdown: A media processing worker consumes the `PhotoUploaded` event, generates thumbnails, and updates the photo's status to 'ready'.

nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Main data flow: posting a photo § shape#3

content.label: 4 · Worker publishes PhotoReady & Feed service updates

nodes.title: Feed Update and Notifications
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Main data flow: posting a photo § text#3

content.markdown: The worker publishes `PhotoReady`. The feed service then adds the photo to followers' feeds and requests the push-notification provider to send alerts.

nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Main data flow: posting a photo § shape#4

nodes.title: Follower Consumption
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Main data flow: posting a photo § text#4

content.markdown: Followers' clients retrieve the updated feed via the gateway and load thumbnails from the CDN.

nodes.title: Sequence Overview
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Main data flow: posting a photo § text#5

content.markdown: This sequence describes the end-to-end process of posting a photo, from client upload to follower notification and display. It involves several services working asynchronously via event publishing.

nodes.title: Key Achievements
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Main data flow: posting a photo § text#6

content.markdown: The entire flow ensures that a user's photo is uploaded, processed into displayable formats, distributed to followers' feeds, and followers are notified, allowing them to view the new content.

nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Design decisions § group#0
Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Design decisions § shape#0
Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Design decisions § text#0

content.markdown: To prevent slow or failed thumbnail jobs from blocking uploads, the upload service and workers interact via a message queue. This introduces a delay of a few seconds for new photos to appear in feeds.

nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Design decisions § shape#1
Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Design decisions § text#1

content.markdown: Clients upload large photo originals (up to 25 MB) directly to object storage using signed URLs. The upload service is responsible for signing the URL and recording the result, avoiding the gateway as a bottleneck.

nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Design decisions § shape#2
Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Design decisions § text#2

content.markdown:
Photo bytes are stored in object storage, while queryable metadata resides in a separate database. This separation is due to differing growth rates and backup requirements for each.

**From the source:** two

nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Design decisions § shape#3
Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Design decisions § text#3

content.markdown: Feed pages are cached for performance, but the metadata database remains the authoritative source of truth. The cache can be flushed at any time without data loss.

nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Design decisions § shape#4
Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Design decisions § text#4

content.markdown: Third-party CDN and push-notification providers are used for delivery, accepting that their outages are beyond direct control.

nodes.title: Status
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › Design decisions § text#5

content.markdown:
* **Queue between upload and processing** — Decided: Implemented to decouple services.
* **Direct upload with signed URLs** — Decided: Implemented.
* **Metadata separate from bytes** — Decided: Implemented for optimized storage and backup.
* **Disposable cache** — Decided: Implemented for performance with data integrity.
* **Buy delivery, don't build it** — Decided: Implemented for leveraging external services.

nodes.title: External Dependencies
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › External dependencies and system boundary § text#0

content.markdown: The CDN and push-notification provider are external services, operated by third parties, and are outside the Pinhole system boundary.

nodes.title: CDN Functionality
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › External dependencies and system boundary § text#1

content.markdown: The CDN retrieves photos and thumbnails from object storage and delivers them to clients from geographically optimized locations.

nodes.title: Push-Notification Provider Functionality
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › External dependencies and system boundary § text#2

content.markdown: The push-notification provider sends alerts to phones. Pinhole initiates these requests but does not control the delivery timing of the alerts.

nodes.title: Internal System Components
nodes.stableKey: Pinhole: high-level design for photo sharing › External dependencies and system boundary § text#3

content.markdown: All other components mentioned in this document, including the gateway, three services, workers, queue, and three stores, are within the Pinhole system boundary and are managed by the Pinhole team.
